source:
Here's a game idea that's unusual enough that it would feel like it was "designed by an AI," but you can still build it in Roblox.
Echo Timeline Obby
Core idea: Every time a player dies, they don't disappear. Instead, an AI-controlled "echo" of their previous run appears and repeats exactly what they did.
Gameplay
Your past selves become moving platforms.
They accidentally press buttons for you.
Some echoes open doors, while others block your path.
Later levels require working with 10-50 previous versions of yourself.
If you make a mistake, it changes the puzzle for your next attempt.
AI twist
Add an AI "Director" that watches how players perform and changes the level in real time:
If players keep failing jumps, it creates a different route.
If they're too fast, it adds harder obstacles.
It learns which paths players choose and generates new sections based on those choices.
Cool features
🌀 Infinite procedurally generated stages.
👻 Ghost replays of every attempt.
🧠 AI-generated puzzle layouts.
🏆 Daily challenge with a unique AI-created map that no one has seen before.
This kind of adaptive game would feel very different from a typical Roblox obby because the level evolves based on how people actually play.
If you'd like, I can also suggest an even more ambitious idea-something that looks like it took a team of professional developers and AI to create.

answers.ask: Nothing was said about how this looks — should the echoes read as ghostly and abstract, or is there a setting behind them?
answers.answer: Use a futuristic abstract sci-fi setting: clean floating platforms, glowing doors and buttons, and dark void surroundings. Echoes should be translucent ghostly versions of the player with a distinct glow.

answers.ask: Should a stage be a flat course, a climb, or a tower? The description is all mechanics.
answers.answer: Make each stage a compact vertical climb/tower so previous-run echoes can visibly cross paths above and below the current player.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: Nothing was said about how this looks — should the echoes read as ghostly and abstract, or is there a setting behind them? A: Use a futuristic abstract sci-fi setting: clean floating platforms, glowing doors and buttons, and dark void surroundings. Echoes should be translucent ghostly versions of the player with a distinct glow.
- [author] shape — Q: Should a stage be a flat course, a climb, or a tower? The description is all mechanics. A: Make each stage a compact vertical climb/tower so previous-run echoes can visibly cross paths above and below the current player.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a compact vertical science-fiction obby stage rising through a dark void, built from clean floating platforms, glowing doors, and luminous floor or wall buttons. Arrange a valid upward route that folds above and below itself so translucent glowing echoes of previous runs can cross the current player’s path, serve as temporary moving footholds, and reach buttons that open later doors. Leave enough shared circulation for 10–50 ghostly echoes in advanced stages without obscuring the current route. Finish at a clear top landing, and preserve the same tower structure for endlessly generated variants.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Obby & Platformer, as explicitly named and defined by the climb. Puzzle is secondary because echoes press buttons and open route gates.

## Shape and preset
Use `course-tower` for a compact route stacked vertically over itself. Start from the Tower Obby preset, retain its ordered track and top endpoint, and replace generic climb and timed obstacles with echo-operated moving footholds, buttons, and gates.

## Config requirements
Use `path-track` for the physics-valid ascending platform chain, `obstacle-moving` for echo-assisted moving footholds, `button-solve` for glowing pressable inputs, `gate-progression` for doors opened by earlier echo actions, and the visible half of `winner-zone` for the top landing.

## Layout requirements
Place the functional half of each `button-solve` beside the route segment its echo can reach, paired with the corresponding door farther along the climb. Place one `winner-zone` at the top landing. Reserve replay paths for 10–50 echoes in advanced stages, but do not turn AI logic into geometry. Omit checkpoints so each failure can produce a full-stage echo.

## Layout components
One compact tower stage contains a bottom start, a vertically folded chain of floating platforms, moving foothold sections, multiple glowing buttons paired with forward doors, crossing routes for echoes above and below, and one top landing. Open void encloses the course. The composition must expose the vertical route and overlapping echo paths clearly.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: route continuity and reachable button-door sequencing must lead before the science-fiction dressing, while no supported authored-plan generator exists for this adaptive obby.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is medium for one compact vertical stage. The theme is abstract futuristic science fiction with luminous ghost echoes and dark void contrast. Use `P6` for a valid platform chain and `P2` because stacked platforms overhang lower route sections.

options.text: A physics-valid ascending chain of floating platforms forming the ordered upward route through the tower.
Echo-assisted moving footholds that previous-run echoes can stand on to create temporary moving steps for the current run.
Glowing pressable floor or wall buttons that echoes can reach to trigger openings later in the climb.
Glowing doors along the climb that open only after earlier echo-pressed buttons have been activated.
A clear top landing at the end of the climb (visible endpoint of the stage).

layout_placement.where: Beside the route segment its echo can reach; paired with the corresponding door farther along the climb.

layout_placement.text: Top landing end area at the summit of the tower.

layout.boundary: Open dark void surrounds/encloses the floating tower course.
layout.theme: Abstract futuristic science fiction with clean floating platforms, glowing doors and buttons, and translucent luminous ghost echoes against a dark void.

notes: Blob specifies omitting checkpoints; no corresponding catalogue option was provided, so it is not represented as an option.
Blob mentions 10–50 ghostly echoes as circulation capacity; echoes are not a catalogue option and are treated as scene dressing rather than an option.
No explicit counts were stated for buttons, doors, moving foothold sections, or platforms, so their counts are -1.
